General Motors Corporation (GM). GM stated that their tomments to the NPRM on market place considerations are applicable to the draft EIS. In commenting on the NPRM, GM stated that they agreed with the description of the types of market shifts which might accompany a high AFES. GM goes further to say that it is the consumer who reacts and this reaction limits what a manufacturer can do to meet an AFES. They state that if the manufacturer must market a certain product that the consumer does not like then the market shift might occur.

Ford Motor Company. Ford stated that their comments to the NPRM on market shifts are applicable to the draft EIS. In commenting on the NPRM, Ford stated that they agreed with the anlysis that led to the conclusion that an AFES set too high would cause the market shifts indicated. Ford stated that the manufacturers cannot control market shifts except for the short term by pricing actions, advertising, and other merchandising techniques. They stated that they are trying to shift demand for certain 1977 engines to use more effectively existing production capacity but they are not certain the attempt will work.
